claim: The Drosophila central brain develops from approximately 100 pairs of bilaterally symmetric neural stem cells called neuroblasts (NBs).
source: The Drosophila central brain develops from approximately 100 pairs of bilaterally symmetric neural stem cells, called neuroblasts (NBs) (Urbach and Technau, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Urbach and Technau, 2003

claim: Most central brain NBs undergo around 100 cell cycles in two neurogenic periods, first building larval networks and then more complex adult neural networks.
source: Most central brain NBs undergo around 100 cell cycles in two neurogenic periods, first building larval networks and then more complex adult neural networks (Truman and Bate, 1988).
evidence: Supported by citation to Truman and Bate, 1988

claim: A typical neuronal lineage consists of serially derived lineage-specific pairs of post-mitotic neurons.
source: A typical neuronal lineage, born from a single NB, consists of serially derived lineage-specific pairs of post-mitotic neurons.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript describing lineage composition

claim: Due to differential Notch signaling, paired neurons made by transient ganglion mother cells (GMCs) can acquire very distinct morphological, physiological, and molecular phenotypes depending on binary sister fates, referred to as A (Non) and B (Noff) fates.
source: Due to differential Notch (N) signaling, the paired neurons, made by transient ganglion mother cells (GMCs), can acquire very distinct morphological, physiological, and molecular phenotypes depending on binary sister fates, referred to as A (Non) and B (Noff) fates (Spana and Doe, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to Spana and Doe, 1996

claim: Within a lineage, neurons of the same A or B fate constitute a hemilineage.
source: Within a lineage, neurons of the same A or B fate constitute a hemilineage (Truman et al., 2010; Shepherd et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Truman et al., 2010 and Shepherd et al., 2019

claim: Temporal patterning allows further neuronal fate diversification within a given hemilineage based on neuronal birth order.
source: Temporal patterning allows further neuronal fate diversification within a given hemilineage based on neuronal birth order (Doe, 2017; Miyares and Lee, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Doe, 2017 and Miyares and Lee, 2019

claim: NB clones are stereotyped with both characteristic cell body positions and distinctive lineage-specific neurite projections.
source: NB clones are stereotyped; they have both characteristic cell body positions and distinctive lineage-specific neurite projections.
evidence: Direct statement describing NB clone characteristics

claim: Using MARCM to induce NB clones in newly hatched larvae, approximately 100 distinct lineages were identified in the fly central brain.
source: Using MARCM (Lee and Luo, 1999) to induce NB clones in newly hatched larvae, we identified ~100 distinct lineages in the fly central brain (Yu et al., 2013; Ito et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yu et al., 2013 and Ito et al., 2013, and reference to MARCM method from Lee and Luo, 1999

claim: Discrete lineage identities arise from the spatially patterned neuroectoderm where NB specification occurs, and involve evolutionarily conserved anteroposterior gap genes and dorsoventral patterning genes.
source: Discrete lineage identities arise from the spatially patterned neuroectoderm where NB specification occurs, and involve evolutionarily conserved anteroposterior gap genes and dorsoventral patterning genes (Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008; Urbach and Technau, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008 and Urbach and Technau, 2008

claim: Individual NBs can be identified in early embryos based on combinatorial expression of various transcription factors.
source: In early embryos, individual NBs can indeed be identified based on combinatorial expression of various transcription factors (TF) (Urbach and Technau, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Urbach and Technau, 2003

claim: Altering the TF code can transform neuronal fate and wiring, suggesting that lineage identity controls aspects of neuronal type and morphology.
source: Altering the TF code can transform neuronal fate and wiring, suggesting that lineage identity controls aspects of neuronal type and morphology (Sen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sen et al., 2014

claim: Only three of the about 100 distinct neuronal lineages have been fully mapped at the single-cell level in adult fly brains: the mushroom body (MB), anterodorsal antennal lobe (ALad1) and lateral antennal lobe (ALl1) lineages.
source: To date, only three of the about 100 distinct neuronal lineages have been fully mapped at the single-cell level in adult fly brains: the mushroom body (MB), anterodorsal antennal lobe (ALad1) and lateral antennal lobe (ALl1) lineages (Lee et al., 1999; Jefferis et al., 2001; Yu et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 1999; Jefferis et al., 2001; Yu et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2012

claim: The four identical MB lineages are composed of only three major KC types.
source: The four identical MB lineages are composed of only three major KC types; moreover, paired KCs from common GMCs show no evidence for binary sister fate determination (Lee et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 1999

claim: Paired KCs from common GMCs show no evidence for binary sister fate determination.
source: The four identical MB lineages are composed of only three major KC types; moreover, paired KCs from common GMCs show no evidence for binary sister fate determination (Lee et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 1999

claim: The two AL NBs produce progeny that rapidly change type (producing upwards of 40 neuron types) and the GMCs generate discrete A/B sister fates.
source: By contrast, the two AL NBs produce progeny that rapidly change type (producing upwards of 40 neuron types) and the GMCs generate discrete A/B sister fates (Yu et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yu et al., 2010 and Lin et al., 2012

claim: In the ALl1 lineage, differential Notch signaling specifies PNs versus LNs.
source: In the ALl1 lineage, differential Notch signaling specifies PNs versus LNs (Lin et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin et al., 2010

claim: The paired PN and LN hemilineages show independent temporal-fate changes, as evidenced by windows with unilateral switches in production of distinct PNs or LNs.
source: Notably, the paired PN and LN hemilineages show independent temporal-fate changes, as evidenced by windows with unilateral switches in production of distinct PNs or LNs (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin et al., 2012

claim: The ALl1 PN hemilineage alternately yields Notch-dispensable AL and Notch-dependent AMMC PNs.
source: Moreover, the ALl1 PN hemilineage alternately yields Notch-dispensable AL and Notch-dependent AMMC PNs (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lin et al., 2012

claim: Cellular diversity—as characterized by gene expression—is higher during development than in mature brains.
source: In fact, cellular diversity—as characterized by gene expression—is higher during development than in mature brains (Li et al., 2017), signifying that the underpinnings of the connectome can be understood by studying development.
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2017

claim: Urbach and Technau reported 21 fly brain NBs expressing Ventral nervous system defective (Vnd), including 13 of the 72 protocerebral NBs, 4 of the 21 deutocerebral NBs, and 4 of the 13 tritocerebral NBs.
source: Urbach and Technau reported 21 fly brain NBs expressing Ventral nervous system defective (Vnd, homolog of the Nkx2 family of homeobox transcription factors). These include 13 of the 72 protocerebral NBs, 4 of the 21 deutocerebral NBs, and 4 of the 13 tritocerebral NBs (Urbach and Technau, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Urbach and Technau, 2003

claim: The study detected 18 stereotyped neuronal lineages with cell bodies within the Drosophila central brain.
source: We detected 18 stereotyped neuronal lineages with cell bodies within the Drosophila central brain (modeled in Figure 1A based on data from Figure 2).
evidence: Direct statement of findings with reference to figures

claim: The 18 detected lineages correspond to the SMPad1, SMPp&v1, SLPpm3, CREa1, CREa2, WEDd1, AOTUv1, AOTUv3, AOTUv4, VLPa2, VESa1, VESa2, ALv1, LALv1, FLAa1, FLAa2, FLAa3, and WEDa1 lineages.
source: These lineages correspond to the SMPad1, SMPp&v1, SLPpm3, CREa1, CREa2, WEDd1, AOTUv1, AOTUv3, AOTUv4, VLPa2, VESa1, VESa2, ALv1, LALv1, FLAa1, FLAa2, FLAa3, and WEDa1 lineages that we previously identified (Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu et al., 2013

claim: The cell body clusters of vnd-GAL4 lineages cover the medial part of the anterior brain surface.
source: The cell body clusters of these vnd-GAL4 lineages cover the medial part of the anterior brain surface (Figure 1A and Figure 2), consistent with Vnd's expression around the midline of the embryonic CNS (https://insitu.fruitfly.org/cgi-bin/ex/report.pl?ftype=1&ftext=FBgn0261930).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 2, and consistent with external database information

claim: The study imaged 5771 brains containing twin-spot clones of the 18 Vnd lineages.
source: We imaged 5771 brains containing twin-spot clones of the 18 Vnd lineages.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental data

claim: The study manually annotated 20,916 clones to specific Vnd lineages in the brain.
source: We manually annotated individual clones (e.g. Figure 1B–D) and ascribed 20,916 clones to specific Vnd lineages in the brain.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: Only 7 of the 18 Vnd lineages (SMPp&v1, CREa1, CREa2, AOTUv1, AOTUv3, AOTUv4, and LALv1) produce two viable hemilineages.
source: In fact, only 7 of the 18 Vnd lineages (SMPp&v1, CREa1, CREa2, AOTUv1, AOTUv3, AOTUv4, and LALv1) produce two viable hemilineages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: The paired neurons across sister Vnd hemilineages consistently exhibit distinct morphology and have different neuropil targets, reflecting Notch-dependent binary sister fates.
source: Regardless of lineage origin, the paired neurons across sister Vnd hemilineages consistently exhibit distinct morphology and have different neuropil targets, reflecting Notch-dependent binary sister fates (Figure 2A–G; see below).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2A–G

claim: The remaining 11 lineages exist as a lone hemilineage, as evidenced by the recovery of only unpaired single-neuron clones that share lineage-specific primary trajectories and often innervate common neuropils.
source: The remaining 11 lineages exist as a lone hemilineage, as evidenced by the recovery of only unpaired single-neuron clones that share lineage-specific primary trajectories and often innervate common neuropils (Figure 2H–R; see below).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2H–R

claim: The study identified 467 morphological neuron types from 25 Vnd hemilineages in the fly central brain.
source: Briefly, we have identified 467 morphological neuron types from 25 Vnd hemilineages in the fly central brain (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Direct statement of findings with reference to supplementary file

claim: The five most heterogeneous hemilineages are: ALv1(A) (46 types), VLPa2(A) (37 types), LALv1B (31 types), LALv1A (29 types), and CREa1A (26 types).
source: The five most heterogeneous hemilineages are: ALv1(A) (46 types), VLPa2(A) (37 types), LALv1B (31 types), LALv1A (29 types), and CREa1A (26 types).
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: The five least heterogeneous hemilineages are: FLAa1(B) (five types), FLAa3(A) (seven types), CREa1B (nine types), SLPpm3(B) (11 types), and VESa1(A) (12 types).
source: The five least heterogeneous are: FLAa1(B) (five types), FLAa3(A) (seven types), CREa1B (nine types), SLPpm3(B) (11 types), and VESa1(A) (12 types).
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: The sister hemilineages exist as spatially separate entities in six of the seven paired Vnd lineages.
source: Notably, the sister hemilineages exist as spatially separate entities in six of the seven paired Vnd lineages.
evidence: Direct statement based on analysis of hemilineage data

claim: Only the LALv1 lineage has an extensively mixed A/B cell body region and an initial common bundle that extends posteriorly before branching into multiple A- and B-specific fascicles.
source: Only the LALv1 lineage has an extensively mixed A/B cell body region and an initial common bundle that extends posteriorly before branching into multiple A- and B-specific fascicles (Figure 2G and X).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2G and X

claim: 12 out of 25 (48%) Vnd hemilineages contain neurons with uniquely exuberant elaborations born at the beginning of larval neurogenesis.
source: All together, we found that 12 out of 25 (48%) Vnd hemilineages contain neurons with uniquely exuberant elaborations born at the beginning of larval neurogenesis.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: Eight hemilineages (32%) terminate with neurons that have drastically reduced domains of elaboration.
source: Contrasting the complexity of early-born neurons, eight hemilineages (32%), SMPad1(A), SLPpm3(B), CREa1B, CREa2B, AOTUv1B, LALv1B, FLAa2(A), and VESa1(A), terminate with neurons that have drastically reduced domains of elaboration.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: Only six (24%) Vnd hemilineages consist of neurons that exclusively belong to a single topological class.
source: Notably, only six (24%) Vnd hemilineages, ALv1(A), CREa2B, FLAa1(B), FLAa3(A), LALv1A, and SMPad1(A), consist of neurons that exclusively belong to a single topological class.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: Six (24%) Vnd hemilineages are composed of three to four topological classes of neurons in addition to the atypical beginning and ending neurons.
source: However, there are also six (24%) Vnd hemilineages, AOTUv4B, LALv1B, SMPp&v1A, SMPp&v1B, VESa1(A), and WEDd1(B), composed of three to four topological classes of neurons in addition to the atypical beginning and ending neurons.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: All LALv1A neurons born after larval hatching project along the same primary track into the CX, including the fan-shaped body (FB), noduli (NO), ellipsoid body (EB), and asymmetric body (AB).
source: Notably, all LALv1A neurons born after larval hatching project along the same primary track into the CX, including the fan-shaped body (FB), noduli (NO), ellipsoid body (EB), and asymmetric body (AB) (Figure 7A–Q).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7A–Q

claim: The LALv1B hemilineage consists of six morphological groups with distinct patterns of neuropil targeting (referred to as IB, PS1, SP, PLP, VLP, and PS2 group).
source: In contrast to the relatively uniform LALv1A hemilineage, the sister hemilineage, LALv1B, consists of six morphological groups with distinct patterns of neuropil targeting (referred to as IB, PS1, SP, PLP, VLP, and PS2 group based on the principal or unique neuropil of innervation) (Figure 7A'–R').
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7A'–R'

claim: 12 of 25 hemilineages yield only one dominant morphological group.
source: There are 11 additional (48% in total) Vnd hemilineages which, like LALv1A, contain only one dominant morphological group.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results (11 additional plus LALv1A = 12 total)

claim: The postembryonic VLPa2(A) hemilineage is exclusively dedicated to the formation of the visual topographic map in the VLP neuropil.
source: In particular, the postembryonic VLPa2(A) hemilineage is exclusively dedicated to the formation of the visual topographic map in the VLP neuropil (Figure 1—source data 1P).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—source data 1P

claim: All the 46 ALv1(A) neuron types, with the exception of the unique first larval-born neuron, uniformly relay olfactory information from the AL to the LH.
source: Analogously, all the 46 ALv1(A) neuron types, with the exception of the unique first larval-born neuron, uniformly relay olfactory information from the AL to the LH (Figure 1—source data 1A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—source data 1A

claim: 13 of 25 hemilineages yield multiple morphological groups targeting discrete neuropils.
source: There are 12 additional (52% in total) Vnd hemilineages which, like LALv1B, contain multiple neuron groups targeting discrete sets of neuropils.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results (12 additional plus LALv1B = 13 total)

claim: The CREa1A and CREa2A hemilineages are indistinguishable from each other.
source: Briefly, we found that each of the CREa1 and CREa2 NBs produces an intricate sequence of PAM neurons (Aso et al., 2014) and that the Non hemlineages, CREa1A and CREa2A, are indistinguishable from each other (compare CREa1A(type) with CREa2A(type) heatmaps in Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—source data 1 and citation to Aso et al., 2014

claim: The two NBs produce two identical series of PAM neurons.
source: This phenomenon indicates that the two NBs produce two identical series of PAM neurons.
evidence: Inference based on the indistinguishability of CREa1A and CREa2A PAM neurons

claim: In each series of PAM neurons, 17 types of PAM neurons were identified based on MB lobe innervation patterns.
source: In each series of PAM neurons, we identified 17 types of PAM neurons based on MB lobe innervation patterns (Figure 11A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 11A

claim: This list covers all 14 previously reported types of PAM neurons plus three undocumented morphological types (r4 <r2, r4r5, and b'2r5).
source: This list covers all 14 previously reported types of PAM neurons plus three undocumented morphological types (r4 <r2, r4r5, and b'2r5).
evidence: Direct statement comparing current findings to previous reports

claim: NBLAST analysis recovered 53 pairs of morphologically related non-sibling neuron types.
source: We selected 326 pairs with similarity scores higher than 0.3 (equivalent to top 3%). To find similar neurons between different hemilineages, we eliminated intra-hemilineage comparisons and recovered 53 pairs of morphologically related non-sibling neuron types.
evidence: Direct statement of NBLAST analysis results

claim: Consolidating interconnected pairs resulted in 16 non-overlapping similarity groups containing 70 Vnd neuron types in total.
source: Consolidating interconnected pairs resulted in 16 non-overlapping similarity groups containing 70 Vnd neuron types in total (Figure 12A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 12A

claim: Eight of the 16 groups can be largely accounted for by the related hemilineages described in manual analysis.
source: NBLAST analysis corroborates our manual analysis as eight of the 16 groups can be largely accounted for by the related hemilineages we describe above (CREa1A/CREa2A: 5, AOTUv4A/LALv1A: 2, and AOTUv3B/AOTUv4B: 1).
evidence: Direct statement comparing NBLAST results to manual analysis

claim: Only two relatively simple hemilineages, CREa1B and FLAa1, display progressive changes in morphology along an entire neuron series.
source: Only two relatively simple hemilineages, CREa1B and FLAa1, display progressive changes in morphology along an entire neuron series.
evidence: Direct statement based on NBLAST analysis of temporal patterns

claim: Various degrees of cyclic changes exist in all other hemilineages.
source: By contrast, various degrees of cyclic changes (indicating recurrent relatedness) exist in all other hemilineages.
evidence: Direct statement based on NBLAST analysis of temporal patterns

claim: Primary trajectories and thus neuropil targets are mainly dependent upon both lineage identity and Notch signaling—that is hemilineage identity.
source: Mapping neuron morphology for 25 hemilineages in this study reveals that primary trajectories and thus neuropil targets are mainly dependent upon both lineage identity and Notch signaling—that is hemilineage identity.
evidence: Inference based on comprehensive analysis of 25 hemilineages

claim: The average length of the main trajectory is significantly greater on the Noff than Non side in only two (CREa1 and SMPp&v1, p-value<0.01) of the seven Vnd lineages composed of dual hemilineages.
source: At the single-cell level, the average length of the main trajectory (defined as the total length of the segmented neuron after pruning branches shorter than 50 microns) is significantly greater on the Noff than Non side in only two (CREa1 and SMPp&v1, p-value<0.01) of the seven Vnd lineages composed of dual hemilineages (Figure 13—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 13—figure supplement 1

claim: The degree (coefficient) of variation in the length of the main trajectory is significantly higher on the Noff than Non side (p-value=0.036 for one-tailed paired T test).
source: First, the degree (coefficient) of variation in the length of the main trajectory is significantly higher on the Noff than Non side (p-value=0.036 for one-tailed paired T test).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of trajectory length data

claim: There exist significantly higher numbers of topological neuronal classes in the B than A hemilineages (p-value=0.023 for one-tailed paired T test).
source: Second, there indeed exist significantly higher numbers of topological neuronal classes in the B than A hemilineages (p-value=0.023 for one-tailed paired T test).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of topological class data

claim: From the 11 Vnd unpaired hemilineages, seven are Non and four are Noff.
source: From the 11 Vnd unpaired hemilineages, seven are Non and four are Noff.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: Notch can promote or suppress neuronal cell death depending on lineage identity.
source: For instance, Notch can promote or suppress neuronal cell death depending on lineage identity.
evidence: Statement based on known Notch signaling properties

claim: Both general topology and terminal arborization seem primarily tailored by the targets innervated.
source: In fact, both general topology and terminal arborization seem primarily tailored by the targets innervated (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Inference based on analysis of neuron morphology data shown in Figure 1—source data 1

claim: Unrelated hemilineages with striking similarities consistently have the same Notch state.
source: Further, unrelated hemilineages with striking similarities (e.g. CREa1A/CREa2A and LALv1A/AOTUv4A) consistently have the same Notch state.
evidence: Observation based on comparison of hemilineages

claim: Notch may directly regulate neuropil targeting, as implicated by the complete segregation of the Non and Noff neuronal processes observed in six of the seven (not LALv1) dual lineages.
source: Nonetheless, Notch may directly regulate neuropil targeting, as implicated by the complete segregation of the Non and Noff neuronal processes observed in six of the seven (not LALv1) dual lineages (Figure 2A–G).
evidence: Speculation based on observation of data shown in Figure 2A–G

claim: Notch can promote cell adhesion, either by acting as a cell adhesion molecule or by upregulating canonical cell adhesion molecules such as integrins.
source: Further, Notch can promote cell adhesion, either by acting as a cell adhesion molecule or by upregulating canonical cell adhesion molecules such as integrins (Murata and Hayashi, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Murata and Hayashi, 2016

claim: Notch may strengthen neurite-neurite affinity, as higher affinity in A hemilineages could suppress neurite defasciculation resulting in more uniform trajectory, and facilitate extension of long neurite fascicles.
source: Here, we speculate that Notch may strengthen neurite-neurite affinity, as higher affinity in A hemilineages could suppress neurite defasciculation resulting in more uniform trajectory (e.g. Figure 2B[green], C[green], F[green], G[green], I, K, L, N), and facilitate extension of long neurite fascicles (e.g. Figure 2I,K,L,M,N).
evidence: Speculation based on observations shown in Figure 2

claim: Reduced affinity in B hemilineages could promote gross diversity through serial defasciculation of primary projections.
source: By contrast, reduced affinity in B hemilineages could promote gross diversity through serial defasciculation of primary projections.
evidence: Speculation based on comparison with A hemilineages

claim: The Cas and Svp embryonic temporal transcription factors are expressed in NBs during early postembryonic neurogenesis and are candidates to promote the uniquely exuberant neurite projections in first-born neurons.
source: The Cas and Svp embryonic temporal transcription factors are expressed in NBs during early postembryonic neurogenesis (Maurange et al., 2008) and are thus candidates to promote the uniquely exuberant neurite projections in first-born neurons.
evidence: Speculation based on known expression patterns from Maurange et al., 2008

claim: Opposing temporal gradients of Imp and Syp RNA binding proteins in cycling NBs have been shown to control neuronal temporal fate in MB, AL, and complex type II lineages as well as global NB termination.
source: Opposing temporal gradients of Imp and Syp RNA binding proteins in cycling NBs have been shown to control neuronal temporal fate in MB, AL, and complex type II lineages as well as global NB termination (Liu et al., 2015; Ren et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2015; Ren et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2017

claim: Imp/Syp are likely to govern long-range temporal patterning of most, if not all, neuronal lineages.
source: Imp/Syp are likely to govern long-range temporal patterning of most, if not all, neuronal lineages.
evidence: Inference based on known roles of Imp/Syp in multiple lineages

claim: Imp and Syp gradients shape the descending protein gradient of Chinmo.
source: Imp and Syp gradients shape the descending protein gradient of Chinmo (Zhu et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2006

claim: Mamo (a temporally patterned terminal selector gene) is selectively expressed in the window defined by both weak Chinmo and abundant Syp in MB and AL lineages.
source: For instance, Mamo (a temporally patterned terminal selector gene) is selectively expressed in the window defined by both weak Chinmo and abundant Syp in MB and AL lineages (Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2019

claim: Dynamic Notch signaling may underlie some alternating temporal fates, as Notch has been shown to control alternate production of AL and AMMC projection neurons in the lateral AL lineage.
source: Dynamic Notch signaling may underlie some alternating temporal fates, as Notch has been shown to control alternate production of AL and AMMC projection neurons in the lateral AL lineage (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Speculation supported by citation to Lin et al., 2012

claim: There likely exist multiple temporal fating mechanisms that act in concert to expand neuron diversity, thus resulting in complex temporal patterns.
source: In sum, there likely exist multiple temporal fating mechanisms that act in concert to expand neuron diversity, thus resulting in complex temporal patterns (Figure 14C).
evidence: Inference based on observed complexity of temporal patterns, illustrated in Figure 14C

claim: Neighboring CREa1 and CREa2 lineages may have arisen from NB duplication followed by a change in midline crossing.
source: These phenomena implicate that neighboring CREa1 and CREa2 lineages may have arisen from NB duplication followed by a change in midline crossing.
evidence: Speculation based on similarities and differences between CREa1 and CREa2 lineages

claim: One way for brain complexity to increase is through lineage duplication and subsequent divergence.
source: Thus, we believe that one way for brain complexity to increase is through lineage duplication and subsequent divergence.
evidence: Inference based on the CREa1/CREa2 example

claim: The observed birth order-dependent neuronal morphogenesis is unlikely due to the environmental differences over the course of larval neurogenesis, since the final neuronal targeting and innervation occur in a rather synchronized manner at the early pupal stage.
source: As to underlying molecular mechanisms, the observed birth order-dependent neuronal morphogenesis is unlikely due to the environmental differences over the course of larval neurogenesis, since the final neuronal targeting and innervation occur in a rather synchronized manner at the early pupal stage.
evidence: Inference based on timing of neuronal development

claim: Neuropil structures in adult Drosophila brains have been extensively characterized, showing stereotypy and enabling alignment of multiple brains.
source: Neuropil structures in adult Drosophila brains have been extensively characterized, showing stereotypy and enabling alignment of multiple brains (Rein et al., 2002; Ito et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rein et al., 2002 and Ito et al., 2014

claim: Systematic efforts in cataloging neurons based on morphology and genetic drivers will soon yield a complete neuron type list for the fly CNS.
source: Further, systematic efforts in cataloging neurons based on morphology and genetic drivers will soon yield a complete neuron type list for the fly CNS (Aso et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Aso et al., 2014

claim: The fly brain connectome is being constructed at the level of individual synapses.
source: Additionally, the fly brain connectome is being constructed at the level of individual synapses (Takemura et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Takemura et al., 2017 and Zheng et al., 2018

claim: Both anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning of the CNS are remarkably conserved from insects to humans.
source: Both anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning of the CNS are remarkably conserved from insects to humans (Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008; Urbach and Technau, 2008), including the tripartite organization of the brain (the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain correspond to the fly's protocerebral, deutocerebral, and tritocerebral neuromeres).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008 and Urbach and Technau, 2008

claim: The tripartite organization of the brain is conserved, with the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain corresponding to the fly's protocerebral, deutocerebral, and tritocerebral neuromeres.
source: Both anteroposterior and dorsoventral patterning of the CNS are remarkably conserved from insects to humans (Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008; Urbach and Technau, 2008), including the tripartite organization of the brain (the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain correspond to the fly's protocerebral, deutocerebral, and tritocerebral neuromeres).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lichtneckert and Reichert, 2008 and Urbach and Technau, 2008

claim: Vnd is the homolog of the Nkx2 family of homeobox transcription factors.
source: Urbach and Technau reported 21 fly brain NBs expressing Ventral nervous system defective (Vnd, homolog of the Nkx2 family of homeobox transcription factors).
evidence: Direct statement of gene homology

claim: The study created a GAL4 driver under the control of endogenous vnd regulatory sequences using gene targeting.
source: To analyze Vnd+ NBs, we created a GAL4 driver under the control of endogenous vnd regulatory sequences using gene targeting (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: Direct statement of methods with citation to Chen et al., 2015

claim: The study derived a Vnd-specific, lineage-restricted LexA driver using a cascade of site-specific recombinases.
source: To immortalize the NB expression of Vnd into the neuronal progeny, we derived a Vnd-specific, lineage-restricted LexA driver using a cascade of site-specific recombinases.
evidence: Direct statement of methods

claim: The study conducted transient clone induction in contiguous 2-hr windows from 18 hr after larval hatching (ALH) to 92 hr ALH and from 22 hr before pupa formation (BPF) to 16 hr after pupa formation (APF).
